verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential relationship between Nystatin and Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3, as multiple pathways indicate that Nystatin targets different proteins that ultimately interact with this transporter. Specifically, Nystatin is linked to Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 2B1, which is targeted by methyl (1R,4S,5R,9S,10S,13R,15S)-15-acetyloxy-5,9-dimethyl-14-methylidenetetracyclo[11.2.1.01,10.04,9]hexadecane-5-carboxylate, and this compound further targets the same transporter. Additionally, Nystatin is also associated with Serine/threonine-protein phosphatase 5, which is targeted by aminohippurate, which in turn targets the same transporter. These findings collectively suggest that Nystatin may influence the activity of the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3 through a series of intermediate targets. The evidence is consistent across different pathways, indicating a possible mechanism by which Nystatin modulates the transporter, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
